proposal.utterance: What BFO category best fits 'the normative force of an obligation'?

entities.label: NormativeForce
entities.rationale: Normative force is the capacity or power of an obligation to bind, compel, or direct action. It is internally grounded in the obligation-bearer relation and is not merely an external label — it is a genuine disposition of the norm (or of the legal/social entity bearing the obligation) that is realized in episodes of compliance, enforcement, or acknowledgment. BFO Disposition (BFO_0000016) best captures this: a disposition inheres in its bearer and is realized in processes, without being a mere quality (measurable property) or role (externally conferred). Contrast: Role (BFO_0000023) would apply if the force were purely externally assigned; Quality (BFO_0000019) would apply if it were a static measurable property; the Disposition captures the directedness and capacity-to-be-realized character of normative force.

relations.rationale: NormativeForce is typed as a subclass of BFO Disposition because it is an internally grounded capacity inhering in a norm-bearer that is realized in processes of compliance or enforcement.
Open question — do not assert yet. NormativeForce may inhere in a LegalObligation individual rather than be a subclass of it. Listing for user confirmation.

open_questions: Should NormativeForce be modeled as inhering IN a LegalObligation instance (i.e., an SDC whose bearer is a LegalObligation individual), or as a property of the agent who bears the obligation?
Is 'normative force' here meant as a type-level class (a kind of disposition) or as a specific individual instance attached to a particular obligation?

Should NormativeForce be distinguished from LegalLegitimacyCondition (already in the ontology as BFO_0000016) or is it a subtype of it? The existing class captures conditions for legitimacy, whereas normative force is the binding power of the obligation itself.

Could normative force also have a Role (BFO_0000023) reading — e.g., the role an obligation plays in practical reasoning — which would make it externally grounded rather than internally grounded? If so, should both a Disposition and a Role subclass be minted?
proposal.rationale_summary: The phrase 'normative force of an obligation' refers to the binding, action-directing capacity that an obligation possesses — the feature in virtue of which it places a genuine demand on an agent. In BFO terms, this is best captured as a Disposition (BFO_0000016): it is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in a bearer (the obligation, or the agent who bears the obligation), is internally grounded (it flows from the nature of the norm and its social/legal grounding, not merely from external labeling), and is realized in processes such as compliance acts, enforcement proceedings, or acknowledgment events. A Quality (BFO_0000019) would not fit because normative force is not simply a measurable property; a Role (BFO_0000023) would not fit cleanly because roles are externally conferred and do not carry the internal-grounding character of normative bindingness. The second relation proposed (subClassOf LegalObligation) is flagged as an open question rather than asserted, because the more precise modeling is likely that NormativeForce inheres in LegalObligation instances via RO_0000052, not that it is a subclass of LegalObligation.
